.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable
- Meaning (from field description on the Deployment concepts page): “.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable is an optional field that specifies the maximum number of Pods that can be unavailable during the update process. The value can be an absolute number (for example, 5) or a percentage of desired Pods (for example, 10%). The absolute number is calculated from percentage by rounding down. The value cannot be 0 if .spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxSurge is 0.”
- Default value: “The default value is 25%.”

.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxSurge
- Meaning (from field description on the Deployment concepts page): “.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxSurge is an optional field that specifies the maximum number of Pods that can be created over the desired number of Pods. The value can be an absolute number (for example, 5) or a percentage of desired Pods (for example, 10%). The value cannot be 0 if maxUnavailable is 0. The absolute number is calculated from the percentage by rounding up.”
- Default value: “The default value is 25%.”

.spec.progressDeadlineSeconds
- Meaning (from field description on the Deployment concepts page under “Progress Deadline Seconds” / links from “.spec.progressDeadlineSeconds” and “failed progressing”): this field specifies the number of seconds the system will wait for a Deployment to make progress (for example, for the minimum number of Pods to become available) before it is considered to have “failed progressing”. Once that deadline is exceeded without progress, the Deployment is treated as failed progressing.
- Default value: the Deployment concepts page describes the semantics of .spec.progressDeadlineSeconds but does not override the API’s default; on this concepts page, no specific numeric default value is stated for .spec.progressDeadlineSeconds.
